title: evented-chunk-playback-notes-2026
content:
Title: Evented chunk playback / repro notes (SSE / chunking / backpressure)
Owner: Maya Thompson
Context: intermittent client-side stalls and truncated SSE events observed in hosted API when load increases. Repro is flaky in dev but we've reproduced consistently behind the nginx ingress in staging. This doc is a scratchpad for commands tried, logs captured, hypotheses, and follow-ups.

Observed symptoms:
- Client (browser or long-lived CLI) sees a long pause (~3–15s) between SSE events, then several events arrive 'bursted' at once.
- Occasionally events are concatenated into one event on the client (missing blank-line separator) or an event is cut off mid-field.
- Server logs show repeated "write returned EPIPE" and some "connection reset by peer" at times of high recv TPS.
- TCP-level retransmits increase during stall windows.

Environment notes:
- Server: Python 3.11, uvloop enabled, aiohttp 3.9.x, running in gunicorn with --worker-class uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker, container runtime runc.
- Ingress: nginx 1.24.0 with default proxy_buffering on.
- Client: curl (mac/linux), browser EventSource, and internal NodeJS fetch SSE client.
- Transfer encoding: chunked (no Content-Length). Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8.

Repro steps I ran (commands):
1) Plain curl directly to pod (bypass nginx):
   curl -N -v "http://10.2.3.45:8080/sse?test=1" -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
   - Observed: smooth stream under same load.

2) curl via nginx ingress (repro shows stalls):
   curl -N -v "https://stg.redwood-inference/internal/sse/test" -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
   - Observe delays and bursts. Capture headers with -v to confirm proxy_http_version: 1.1 and Transfer-Encoding: chunked.

3) curl with --no-buffer (same as -N), also tried --http2: sometimes differences.

4) Python client (to mimic internal SDK):
   async def fetch():
       async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
           async with s.get(url) as r:
               async for line in r.content:
                   print(repr(line))
   - Behavior: stalls align with nginx path.

5) Netcat test to server (manual chunk boundaries):
   printf 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n5\r\ndata:\x20one\n\n0\r\n\r\n' | nc 10.2.3.45 8080
   - Works when direct; via nginx the same set of small chunks got buffered and delivered grouped.

Quick logs (snips):
- server: "WARNING write() failed: [Errno 32] Broken pipe while streaming to client"
- nginx access log: many 200s but request_time shows spikes matching client stalls (e.g. request_time 12.432).
- tcpdump: shows multiple small TCP segments followed by a pause, then ACKs/bursts.

Experiments tried and results:
1) Disable nginx proxy buffering for the route: proxy_buffering off;
   - Result: immediate improvement. Client got events without long waits.
   - Notes: strongly indicates proxy buffering is the core cause.

2) Ensure nginx proxy_http_version 1.1 and proxy_set_header Connection "";
   - Result: required for chunked streaming over upstream keepalive; otherwise nginx attempted to buffer until end.

3) Turn off gzip on upstream in nginx (proxy_set_header Accept-Encoding "");
   - Result: small improvement; with gzip enabled nginx sometimes buffers to compress.

4) On server, explicitly flush after every event (aiohttp: await resp.write(event_bytes); await resp.drain())
   - Result: necessary but not sufficient when nginx buffering is on. If proxy buffering off, this is sufficient.

5) Try adding double-newline separators and always end events with "\n\n";
   - Result: helped some client parsers but did not fix stall. This is more robustness than fix.

6) Test with Golang minimal SSE server behind same ingress (net/http Flush() called).
   - Result: same stall profile when proxy_buffering on.

Suspected causes (ordered):
- Primary: nginx proxy_buffering combined with small chunk sizes causes buffering until buffer thresholds reached, leading to burst delivery.
- Secondary: gzip compression at proxy causing additional buffering to reach compression window.
- Tertiary: socket-level Nagle/CORK behavior—absence of TCP_NODELAY might coalesce writes on server side.
- Also consider client HTTP/2 support in ingress path causing multiplexing-related stalls.

Possible fixes / mitigations:
- On nginx ingress: set proxy_buffering off for SSE routes; ensure proxy_http_version 1.1 and proxy_set_header Connection ""; disable gzip.
- On server: always call drain/flush after write; write larger events when possible (group 2–3 small events into one chunk).
- SDK: expose an option to set "no-buffer" / force chunking-friendly headers when going through known proxies.
- For long-term: add an ingress test that asserts sub-100ms p95 delivery for one-line SSE events under baseline load.

Commands to reproduce for SRE to run quickly:
- tcpdump capture on pod and ingress to compare timings:
  sudo tcpdump -i any -w sse-stall.pcap host 10.2.3.45 and port 8080
- curl direct vs via ingress and timestamp lines:
  curl -N "http://10.2.3.45:8080/sse/test" | ts '%H:%M:%.S' > direct.log &
  curl -N "https://stg.redwood-inference/internal/sse/test" | ts '%H:%M:%.S' > via-ingress.log &
- quick nginx check: (on ingress) curl -sS localhost:8080/nginx_status && grep -x "proxy_buffering" /etc/nginx/conf.d/*.conf || true

Next steps / TODOs:
- Collect pcap for both paths and attach to INFR-3421.
- Add unit to e2e tests: small SSE events at 1 RPS produce <=200ms inter-event p95.
- Ask platform infra to set proxy_buffering off for SSE endpoints as a short-term fix.
- Investigate whether envoy (control plane) or cloud LB additionally buffers small chunks for HTTP/1.x vs HTTP/2.

Notes to self:
- If you see burst delivery but direct path OK, check any intermediate L7 proxies first.
- Watch out for compression + chunked combinations — gzip often forces buffering.
- Use tcpdump + Wireshark to inspect actual chunk boundaries (Content-length of chunked frame is visible).

Scratch ideas to test later:
- Try sending explicit chunk sizes > 1024 bytes to see if buffer thresholds change behavior.
- Reproduce under simulation of bursty backend (k6 / vegeta) to validate under load.
- Trace strace write() timing on server to ensure writes and flushes occur when expected.

Unresolved questions:
- Why did we see occasional EPIPE on server while direct curl was fine? Possibly due to client timeout in client-side SDK or intermediary closing the socket. Need pcap to confirm who sent FIN.
- Does cloud LB in front of nginx reassemble/suppress chunking differently for HTTP/2?

If anyone else looking at this: add notes below when you try something. This is a messy repro — most likely fix is nginx config (proxy_buffering off) but we need to be careful about performance impact if we disable buffering globally.

-- Maya
